$comment: Advisories we have looked at and decided to carry, each with the reason and a
review date. Anything NOT listed here fails the gate — that is the point: the
old check compared three hardcoded rules and passed the mermaid prototype
An entry is a decision, not a mute. 'reason' has to say why the vulnerable path
is unreachable HERE, not that the package is popular or the severity looks low.
When 'review' passes, the gate warns; that is the prompt to re-check reachability
rather than extend the date reflexively.

allow.reason: Reached only through concurrently, which this repo runs from the electron:dev script with hardcoded literal arguments. No caller passes user or agent input to it, and it is devDependency-only so it never ships.
The shell-quote path above; concurrently itself adds no new sink. devDependency, electron:dev only.
Both advisories need a precondition we do not create: a SOCKS5 ProxyAgent, or a shared response cache across principals. discord.js and jsdom use plain HTTPS with no proxy agent configured.

No advisory of its own; flagged purely as a path to undici. The preconditions there (a SOCKS5 ProxyAgent, or a cache shared across principals) are the ones that would have to hold, and discord.js configures neither.
No advisory of its own; flagged purely as a path to undici, and it issues plain HTTPS requests with no proxy agent, so the SOCKS5 and shared-cache preconditions never hold.
Requires calling the non-secure generator with a negative or zero size. Reached only via postcss at build time, which passes a fixed positive length.
sourceMappingURL arbitrary read needs attacker-controlled CSS at build time. Our CSS is repository content; a writer with that access already has the tree.
Same sourceMappingURL class as postcss, same build-time-only reachability.
Arbitrary read applies to the esbuild DEVELOPMENT SERVER on Windows. We use esbuild as a bundler; the dev server is never started in this repo.
Dev-server-only, and the launch-editor UNC disclosure additionally needs Windows. Production builds do not run the dev server.
DoS applies when an INVALID limit value silently disables size enforcement. We pass no limit, so the default stays in force.
